title: Strange Luttinger liquids in a cavity-embedded one-dimensional electronic chain
authors: Danh-Phuong Nguyen, Christophe Mora, Cristiano Ciuti
abstract: We study a one-dimensional electronic chain coupled to a homogeneous quantized vacuum field and electron-electron interactions. In the absence of the latter, we derive a low-energy effective description in the presence of light-matter coupling, which we identify as a strange Luttinger liquid. Although it retains a formal resemblance to conventional Luttinger liquid theory, the coupling to the quantum field qualitatively modifies the low-energy sector and breaks the standard velocity relation underlying Luttinger universality. For finite electron-electron interactions, we recover a phase diagram featuring several phases as a function of interaction strength and hopping amplitude, including a phase hosting Majorana-like zero modes. Using exact diagonalization, we compute observables that characterize the phase boundaries and show that the cavity field significantly shifts them. We also study the fate of Majorana-like states under the influence of the cavity field, highlighting their modification by light-matter coupling. Finally, we investigate whether the strange Luttinger liquid description identified in the noninteracting regime continues to hold when electron-electron interactions are introduced.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes a one-dimensional electronic chain coupled to an optical cavity field and subject to electron interactions. It establishes that the light-matter coupling fundamentally alters the low-energy physics, leading to a 'strange Luttinger liquid' description. The authors map out phase diagrams showing how this cavity interaction modifies known quantum phases, including those hosting Majorana-like zero modes.
main_problem: The study investigates the low-energy physics of a one-dimensional electronic chain coupled to a quantized vacuum field, aiming to characterize deviations from standard Luttinger liquid theory.
main_result: The coupling to the cavity field creates a 'strange Luttinger liquid' in the non-interacting limit, breaking conventional velocity relations; furthermore, electron-electron interactions lead to a phase diagram featuring Majorana-like zero modes whose boundaries are shifted by the cavity field.
method: The analysis employs bosonization techniques for low-energy effective descriptions and utilizes exact diagonalization (ED) for finite interaction strengths to map out quantum phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The system is a tight-binding electronic chain embedded in an optical cavity, described by a Hamiltonian incorporating light-matter coupling via the Peierls substitution and electron-electron interactions ($U$).
key_observables: Low-energy excitation spectrum, local density of states (LDOS), charge susceptibilities ($\chi$), and dressed bosonic velocities ($	ilde{v}_S, 	ilde{v}_N, 	ilde{v}_J$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$), light-matter coupling strength ($g$), cavity frequency ($\omega_c$), and filling level (half-filling).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving low-energy effective Hamiltonians via perturbation theory in the coupling $g$ and assuming a large but finite chain length.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate electronic phase diagrams showing transitions between Luttinger liquid, Charge Density Wave (CDW), and Phase Separation (PS) phases as functions of interaction strength and cavity coupling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the non-interacting case ($U=0$) to establish the 'strange' nature of the LL. It then extends this analysis using ED for finite $U$, mapping out phase diagrams, and finally investigating how interactions modify the low-energy description derived from cavity coupling.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it merges concepts from quantum optics (cavity QED) with strongly correlated electron physics (Luttinger liquids), providing a mechanism to engineer unconventional quantum states in 1D systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Characteristic velocities of the strange Luttinger liq- uid, normalized by the Fermi velocity, as functions of the cavity coupling g. Solid lines indicate values obtained from Eq. (13), while open symbols correspond to exact velocities calculated directly from the tight-binding model given by Eq. (5). The sound velocity of the collective excitations is given by ¯v(0) S , while ¯v(0) N and ¯v(0) J characterize the propagation ve- locities of density and current fluctuations, respectively. The parameter λ(0) 1 quantifies the cavity-induced band squeezing. Other parameters: N = 500, Ne/N = 1/4, ωc/t = 10.

FIG. 2. Top panel: Real part of the correlation function G(0, τ). Bottom panel: Real part of G(x, 0). G(x, τ) mea- sures the propagation of a fermionic excitation between the spacetime points (0, 0) and (x, τ). Both functions are calcu- lated without (g = 0) and with (g = 2.0) light-matter in- teraction. Inset in both panels display the maxima of the correlation functions on a logarithmic scale, with slope α(g). Other parameters: N = 500, Ne/N = 1/2, ωc/t = 10.

FIG. 3. Electronic phase diagram at half-filling, plotted as a function of U/t and g for N = 12, ωc/t = 10. Left panel shows χ2 for LL-PS transition, while right panel shows χ1 for LL-CDW transition. In both panels, the cross markers indicate the numerical maxima, while the green dashed lines represent extrapolated results.

FIG. 4. Top: Local density of states An(ω) at half-filling for U/t = −2 in the absence of light-matter coupling. Bottom: Edge spectral weight W(U, g) at half-filling as a function of U/t and g. Other parameters: N = 12, ωc/t = 10, Γ = 0.3× level spacing πt/N. The spectral functions are shown in arbi- trary units, and are normalized to their respective maxima.
